extracted.intended_audience: clinical and public-health researchers, instrument developers, and clinicians interested in measurement reliability and validation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical examples for designing, testing, and reporting inter-rater (and related) reliability and validity of clinical, observational, and assessment instruments across settings. Emphasis on statistics (kappa, ICC), training, translation, instrument design, and methods to reduce rater variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess agreement between different raters/observers applying the same instrument or checklist (reported using kappa, weighted kappa, ICCs, percentage agreement as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many studies report unadjusted or weighted kappa, ICCs, Fleiss kappa, or percentage agreement; report the specific statistic used and interpret it alongside raw agreement. Provide per-item and overall agreement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrarater (test-retest) reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess consistency of the same rater over time (test-retest or intrarater agreement), often with repeated scoring sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kappa or correlation coefficients for intrarater agreement; include time between sessions (e.g., 1 week) and any training between sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate agreement statistics (kappa, weighted kappa, ICC, percent agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the statistic suited to the data type (e.g., weighted kappa for ordinal scales, ICC for continuous/rating-scale totals, Fleiss kappa for multi-rater situations) and report confidence intervals where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret kappa with caution (base-rate problems) and present percent agreement in tandem; explicitly state weighting scheme for weighted kappa (e.g., linear weighting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: When instruments have multi-item scales, report internal consistency (e.g., Cronbach's alpha) for subscales and total scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give alpha with confidence intervals and interpret in context (e.g., alpha = 0.83–0.99 reported for different Q-DIO subscales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-retest reliability (temporal stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the stability of instrument scores over time in unchanged participants using test-retest designs and appropriate coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report time interval and correlation coefficients; where items show low test-retest reliability, identify and consider revising them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct, concurrent, and discriminant validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish validity by showing the instrument discriminates between known groups, correlates with established measures, or aligns with expected constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: correlate new scale with Rickets Severity Scale or functional measures; demonstrate the tool discriminates across store types or income neighborhoods; report statistical significance and effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion validity and diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, compare instrument diagnoses/scores with a gold-standard reference (e.g., SCID-II) and report sensitivity, specificity, and kappa for diagnostic convergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cutoff used, sensitivity/specificity values, and kappa for agreement with the standard; interpret diagnostic convergence (e.g., moderate kappa = 0.631).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: For instruments used in other languages/cultures, conduct forward translation, back-translation, critical review, pilot testing, and psychometric testing in the target setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the translation workflow, pilot testing, and report inter-rater/intrarater reliability and internal consistency of the translated version (e.g., ICDSC Swedish translation with weighted kappa = 0.92).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rater training (e.g., standardized training sessions or electronic modules) and document rater experience level, as both affect reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomize assessor order and blind second assessors where possible; single training session or module can improve reliability (AMAT example); experienced analysts produced higher agreement in PATH observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding and randomization of assessor order
rubrics_metrics.description: Design assessment procedures so that second (or other) assessors are blinded to prior findings and order of assessors is randomized when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: second assessor blinded to first rater's findings and assessor order randomized to reduce bias in paired ratings (ergonomics checklist study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of central quality control / central review
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement central monitoring or a central review process with source documentation and structured narratives to reduce inter-rater variation in outcome scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GOSE alternate rating system combined with central quality control produced substantially higher agreement (weighted kappa up to 0.97); central review allows adjudication and documentation of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization of instrument administration (protocols/standard operating procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and apply standardized administration procedures (task analyses, rating matrices, exploring sequence and technique) to increase reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ESSCAT developed from task analysis and consensus-defined minimum standards; faculty calibration training used prescribed exploring sequences for calculus detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item-level analysis and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Report reliability at the level of individual items and revise or remove items with poor reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K-PeCS and AMAT highlighted particular items with low kappa (e.g., sit up K = .16) and recommended further refinement; present per-item kappa/correlation to identify weak items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement error and confidence intervals (SEM, 95% CI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report standard error of measurement (SEM) and confidence intervals for total scores and important subscales to contextualize observed differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMAT reported SEM and 95% CI range so clinicians/researchers can judge meaningful change; include these when proposing cutoffs or minimal detectable change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of objective/instrumented measures when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: When visual judgment is inconsistent, supplement or replace with instrumental measures (e.g., spectrophotometer for color matching) to improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual tooth shade matching had moderate-to-high inconsistency, whereas VITA Easyshade spectrophotometer showed substantially better intra- and inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling design to avoid low variability (base-rate) problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sample variability is adequate for reliability analysis; homogeneous samples can produce low kappa despite high percent agreement (the base-rate problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret low kappa alongside percent agreement; select samples with known variability where possible to avoid misleading kappa results (Irish NMDS discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of observation modality and feasibility assessment (in-person vs virtual)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using observational methods (e.g., SSO), compare and validate in-person versus virtual (e.g., Google Street View) data collection for reliability and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parcel-level SSO via Google Street View achieved substantial inter-rater agreement (>70% items with substantial agreement) and may be feasible for high-resolution neighborhood measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of video/source documentation for reliability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Record performances (videos, radiograph pairs, structured narratives) to permit multi-rater scoring, intrarater retesting, and centralized adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos were used to establish inter-rater reliability in ESSCAT and AMAT; radiograph pairs were scored by multiple pediatric radiologists for RGI-C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design instruments based on existing guidelines and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Build observational checklists and assessment tools grounded in authoritative guidelines and up-to-date empirical evidence to increase content validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ergonomics checklist was designed comparable to government guidelines and supplemented with empirical evidence; this aided acceptability and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report convergent/divergent correlations with external outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that instrument scores relate appropriately to external measures of function, disability, or other clinical outcomes (convergent validity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RGI-C scores correlated significantly with RSS, global function, disability, endurance, and growth measures; reporting these correlations supports validity claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability / ease of administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and report the ease of administration, time-efficiency, and applicability of the instrument to the intended clinical or field setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICDSC Swedish translation noted ease of administration and applicability to the ICU setting; feasibility findings (e.g., parcel-level virtual SSO) should be reported alongside reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus development and stakeholder consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use national consultation or stakeholder input to derive minimum performance standards and refine rating matrices or checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESSCAT used national consultation and consensus to define minimum standards, which contributed to content validity and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine scales with relevant physiological/clinical variables to improve prognostic value
rubrics_metrics.description: When scales alone have limited predictive power, combine them with physiological or clinical parameters in multivariable models to enhance prognostic performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coma scales poorly predicted outcome alone in Nepali children, but combining scores with parameters like systolic blood pressure improved prediction.
